newsitem.title: USA: Plains feedlot cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains feedlot cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle markets Tuesday were inactive amid limited packer buying interest, according to feedlot sources.

There were a few packer bids at $69.00 per cwt, which matched top prices from a week ago. But cattle feeders passed the bids and priced cattle at $71.00 to $72.00. Several said they anticipated sales at $70.00 by Wednesday or Thursday.
Prices this week were expected to be supported by tight numbers of cattle ready to be marketed in showlists that also contained a number of lighter-weight cattle, the sources said.
Feedlot cattle prices also were expected to be underpinned by outlooks for hefty beef demand over the just-completed Labor Day holiday weekend.
If beef usage was active, renewed retail buying could lend support to boxed beef prices and generate stronger demand for the feedlot cattle, market sources said.
Boxed beef prices at near midday Tuesday were quoted down $0.07 to up $0.13 per cwt on 38 loads of fabricated cuts sold, according to USDA.
